source_attestations.note: Approval-ready verification; rules sections 5–12 re-checked against Oracle, rulings and CR

summary:
Each Nathan attack exiles every player's top card and lets you cast one of them during the trigger. His mana fixing covers only spells you don't own. The list adds more triggers (Roaming Throne on Rogue, Firebender Ascension, Karlach), pays with firebending (Fire Nation Palace, Azula), and rewards casting from exile or casting stolen spells (Wild-Magic Sorcerer, Nalfeshnee, Gonti, Tasha, Don Andres). No Spellbook lines.

Rules surprises: your own top card is exiled for good if you don't cast it; Passionate Archaeologist works on Nathan from the 99; Azula's copies don't trigger the stolen-spell payoffs. One flag: Dauthi Voidwalker starves Tinybones.

interactions.title: Attack trigger: one spell from the exiled tops, cast during resolution; the rest stay exiled
interactions.ruling: When Nathan attacks, the top card of every library, yours included, is exiled. While the trigger resolves, you may cast one spell from among them. You cast it during the resolution, so card-type timing is ignored. Sorceries and creatures work in combat, and the spell goes on the stack above the rest of the trigger. You still pay its costs. Lands can't be chosen. Cards you don't cast stay exiled for good, so this also exiles your own top card. Etali, Primal Storm works the same way, but casts any number free. Its rulings cover the timing.
interactions.short: Cast one exiled spell during resolution (timing ignored, costs paid); the rest stay exiled forever.

oracle.quote: Whenever Nathan Drake attacks, exile the top card of each player's library. You may cast a spell from among those cards.

rulings.quote: If you cast any of the exiled cards, you do so as part of the resolution of the triggered ability. You can't wait to cast them later in the turn. Timing permissions based on a card's type are ignored, and the spells resolve before blockers are declared.
Any cards not cast, including land cards, remain in exile. They can't be cast on later turns, even if Etali attacks again.

source.quote: A land exiled by Nathan cannot be chosen as the spell because lands are not spells.

interactions.title: Mana fixing covers only spells you don't own and stolen permanents' abilities
interactions.ruling: Nathan lets you spend mana as though it were any color, but only for spells you don't own and for abilities of permanents you control but don't own. Your own exiled card gets no fixing, so a {U}{U} card still needs blue. Thieving Varmint's mana works the same way: only for spells you don't own. Like all "as though any color" effects, this changes how you pay, not the cost.

oracle.quote: You may spend mana as though it were mana of any color to cast spells you don't own or to activate abilities of permanents you control but don't own.
{T}, Pay 1 life: Add two mana of any one color. Spend this mana only to cast spells you don't own.

source.quote: it does not turn the controller's own exiled top card into a five-color spell.

interactions.title: Firebending first: Fire Nation Palace and Fire Lord Azula pay for the stolen spell
interactions.ruling:
Firebending triggers when its creature attacks, just like Nathan's ability. Put the firebending trigger on top so its {R} resolves first and stays until end of combat. Then spend it on the spell Nathan lets you cast, as any color if you don't own the spell.
- **Fire Nation Palace:** {1}{R},{T} gives Nathan firebending 4 before combat. It enters untapped only if you control a basic land.
- **Fire Lord Azula:** if she's attacking too, she copies the stolen spell. The copy isn't cast, so cast triggers don't fire again, and a permanent spell's copy becomes a token.
interactions.short: Stack firebending above Nathan's trigger; Azula copies whatever Nathan lets you cast.

oracle.quote: {1}{R}, {T}: Target creature you control gains firebending 4 until end of turn. (Whenever it attacks, add {R}{R}{R}{R}. This mana lasts until end of combat.)
Whenever you cast a spell while Fire Lord Azula is attacking, copy that spell. You may choose new targets for the copy. (A copy of a permanent spell becomes a token.)

rulings.quote: The copy is created on the stack, so it's not "cast." Abilities that trigger when a player casts a spell won't trigger.
Mana from firebending abilities isn't lost until you leave combat and go to your second main phase. It can be used at any time during combat, even after combat damage has been dealt.

source.quote: The controller can put the firebending trigger above Nathan's trigger, resolve it for four red mana, and then use that mana on an eligible spell cast during Nathan's resolving trigger.

interactions.title: More Nathan triggers: Roaming Throne (Rogue), Firebender Ascension, Karlach
interactions.ruling:
Three ways to get more Nathan triggers:
- **Roaming Throne:** name Rogue (Nathan is a Human Rogue) and his attack trigger triggers twice. Each instance exiles its own set of top cards and allows one cast.
- **Firebender Ascension:** gets a quest counter whenever an attacking creature's own trigger fires, such as Nathan's or the Soldier's firebending. At 4+ counters it copies the trigger. The copy goes above the original and resolves first.
- **Karlach:** if you attack in the first combat, attackers untap, gain first strike, and you get one more combat in which Nathan attacks again. There's no extra main phase in between.
interactions.short: Throne (Rogue) doubles the trigger; Ascension copies it; Karlach adds a second attack.

oracle.quote: If a triggered ability of another creature you control of the chosen type triggers, it triggers an additional time.
Whenever you attack, if it's the first combat phase of the turn, untap all attacking creatures. They gain first strike until end of turn. After this phase, there is an additional combat phase.

rulings.quote: Firebender Ascension's ability will always go on the stack on top of the triggered ability that caused it to trigger. The copy it creates will be created on the stack on top of the original triggered ability and the copy will resolve before that ability.

Notably, the triggered ability of Karlach doesn't give you any additional main phases. This means that you will move directly from the end of combat step of one combat phase to the beginning of combat step of the next one.

source.quote: Choosing **Rogue** includes Nathan Drake, whose type line is Human Rogue.

interactions.title: Cast-from-exile payoffs: Wild-Magic Sorcerer, Nalfeshnee, Passionate Archaeologist, Interdimensional Web Watch
interactions.ruling:
Nathan's casts come from exile, so these all trigger:
- **Wild-Magic Sorcerer:** the first spell you cast from exile each turn has cascade. Cascade digs your own library, and its free spell resolves first.
- **Nalfeshnee:** copies each spell cast from exile. A permanent copy gets haste and is sacrificed at end step.
- **Passionate Archaeologist:** a Background, but it works from the 99. It gives commander creatures you own (Nathan) "whenever you cast a spell from exile, deal damage equal to its mana value to target opponent".
- **Interdimensional Web Watch:** its mana can only be spent on spells from exile.

oracle.quote: The first spell you cast from exile each turn has cascade. (When you cast your first spell from exile, exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card that costs less. You may cast it without paying its mana cost. Put the exiled cards on the bottom in a random order.)
Commander creatures you own have "Whenever you cast a spell from exile, this creature deals damage equal to that spell's mana value to target opponent."

rulings.quote: The first spell you cast from exile each turn will have cascade, even if it's not the first spell you've cast that turn.

interactions.title: Spells-you-don't-own payoffs: Gonti, Tasha, Vaan, Don Andres
interactions.ruling:
These trigger when you cast a stolen card:
- **Gonti, Night Minister:** a Treasure.
- **Tasha:** a 3/3 Demon.
- **Vaan:** +1/+1 counters on your Scouts, Pirates and Rogues.
- **Don Andres:** two tapped Treasures, but only for noncreature spells. He also gives stolen creatures +2/+2, menace and deathtouch.

Your own exiled top card doesn't count for any of them. Azula's copies of stolen spells don't trigger them either, because copies aren't cast.

oracle.quote: Whenever a player casts a spell they don't own, that player creates a Treasure token.
Whenever you cast a noncreature spell you don't own, create two tapped Treasure tokens.

interactions.title: Dauthi Voidwalker starves Tinybones
interactions.ruling: Dauthi Voidwalker exiles, with a void counter, any card that would go to an opponent's graveyard. Tinybones casts nonland permanent cards from an opponent's graveyard, so with Voidwalker out it has nothing to take. Voidwalker can sacrifice itself to play one void card free, which partly makes up for it. Don't plan on both at once.

flag.note: Dauthi Voidwalker's replacement keeps opponents' graveyards empty, turning off Tinybones' combat-damage cast.

oracle.quote: If a card would be put into an opponent's graveyard from anywhere, instead exile it with a void counter on it.
Whenever Tinybones deals combat damage to a player, you may cast target nonland permanent card from that player's graveyard, and mana of any type can be spent to cast that spell.

interactions.title: Haste and evasion: Arena of Glory, Shizo, Brotherhood Regalia
interactions.ruling:
Nathan triggers on attack, so damage isn't needed, but he's only a 3/2 first striker:
- **Arena of Glory:** pay {R}, then tap and exert it for {R}{R}. If that mana is spent on Nathan, he has haste the turn he's cast. It enters untapped only if you control a Mountain.
- **Shizo:** {B},{T} gives a legendary creature fear.
- **Brotherhood Regalia:** equip legendary {1}. The creature is unblockable and has ward {2}.

oracle.quote: Equipped creature has ward {2}, is an Assassin in addition to its other types, and can't be blocked.
{R}, {T}, Exert this land: Add {R}{R}. If any of that mana is spent on a creature spell, it gains haste until end of turn.

source.quote: When Arena mana is spent on Nathan, Nathan can gain haste and attack immediately
